correctness.rationale: The unique greedy arch factorization exactly computes subsequence universality. For theta-symmetric words, mirror prefix and suffix arches leave a central remainder; a new arch occurs iff the union of the remainder support and its involution image (plus the fixed center in the odd case) equals the whole alphabet. A proper support with f fixed points and d two-cycles has exactly the E and O counts shown, yielding the rational bivariate series. The minimal lengths/counts are its lowest-degree coefficients. The two standalone scripts verify independent finite cases but are not substituted for this proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The claim is not the pure reversal or fixed-point-free corollary. Unlike either endpoint case, it evaluates both mixed support conditions and all bivariate coefficients. The proof adapts standard arch machinery but includes a fresh orbit-dependent two-center enumeration. The central distinction is the exact f,d-dependent count, not an assertion of a new definition of universality.

originality.rationale: The theorem is expressly restricted to mixed involutions f>=1,d>=1. Available prior descriptions cover ordinary reversal, fixed-point-free reversal-complement, unrestricted universal words, or involutive conjugacy; their stated results do not evaluate this mixed orbit-type distribution or its f-dependent odd midpoint coefficient. The original-looking part is the complete mixed f,d support enumeration, not the borrowed arch machinery. Absolute priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: An unindexed or otherwise inaccessible all-involution enumeration may already state an equivalent bivariate formula.
Closely related follow-on work or an unpublished thesis might contain a stronger generalization; no total literature-uniqueness proof is asserted.

value.rationale: An involution with fixed symbols and transposed pairs is the natural missing mixed orbit regime. The exact rational series classifies every indexed theta-symmetric word jointly by length and scattered-subsequence universality, giving explicit minimum lengths and counts of all extremizers. This is an exact complete natural family rather than an arbitrary finite slice, and it isolates the nontrivial role of a fixed center. It is relevant to symmetric word generation, though not a code-performance or molecular-stability claim.
